input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: The second § 12.4 binds Customer (our party) with an undefined-scope, worldwide non-compete extending 24 months post-term, covering development, marketing, sale and even acquisition of any competing product or service. That is past the walk-away line (post-term non-compete over 12 months and undefined "competes with Vendor" scope) and contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges Customer made no non-compete commitment. Preferred position is deletion; § 12.3 already preserves our freedom to operate, so no replacement language is needed. Fallback (single named product, term only, 12-month cap, internal development and acquisition carve-outs) is offered in the comment.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the 24-month, all-territory non-compete because we cannot accept restrictions on the products or services we develop, buy, or sell, and it directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have given no non-compete commitment. If Vendor needs protection for a specific offering, we could consider a restriction limited to one named competing product during the term only (no more than 12 months), with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Delete the non-compete imposed on Customer in § 12.4.
